brief: Strong US data this week (University of Michigan consumer sentiment ticked up, durable goods orders beat consensus, and S&P flash PMIs surged) pushed Goldman's 3Q26 GDP tracker up 10bp to +3.4% and drove 10-year Treasury yields up 20bp to 5.17%, even as economists caution the PMI strength may partly reflect nominal bias rather than real activity. Goldman argues rates above 5% and the AI boom are not actually unprecedented: markets performed well in prior high-rate regimes (1990s), and this year's rate rise has not stifled equities (S&P +13% ytd), GDP, or investment. On AI, Goldman estimates the six major hyperscalers (GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META, ORCL, SPCX) must generate a combined ~$1.42tn of cumulative CY2028-30 revenue to clear a 15% ROIC hurdle, implying near-term return compression that Goldman frames as a natural investment-cycle consequence, not poor AI economics. Hyperscaler valuations have de-rated to a 10-year low even as GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN, and SPCX show emerging AI profitability, and Meta previewed continued Muse expansion (commerce, payments, security features) and a hardware pivot toward glasses.
